name: Muirthemne

attributes.attribute: a plain south of Dundalk in the old tale
the field of the win of the Tuatha De Danann over the Fir Bolg
the gate by which the Milesians took the land

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Muirthemne is a great plain that holds the old story of Ireland. The plain spread to the south of the town of Dundalk and opened toward the east. There the races of the island fought for the right to rule it. The folk of the goddess Danu, the Tuatha de Danann, beat the Fir Bolg in battle on that ground. That win did not hold forever. Later the Milesians came across the water and drove the Tuatha de Danann from the land. Muirthemne is thus the field where the masters of Ireland changed in the old tale.
